speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: asked	the Minister for Health whether there are ways to help families who are unable to qualify for additional Government subsidies to pay for outpatient medical fees that may cost thousands of dollars even after basic Government subsidies, such as that for MRIs, CT scans and blood tests.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: With Government subsidies, the cost of these treatments is typically lower than "thousands of dollars".

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: So, the median was $260; the 90th percentile bill size was $560.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: In 2015, more than eight in 10 patients who used MediSave for outpatient scans did not fully utilise their withdrawal limits.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This $200 is on top of the MediSave limits for non-cancer scans and cancer scans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: In addition, MediShield Life provides coverage for outpatient chemotherapy, radiotherapy and renal dialysis, which are more expensive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Together, these schemes ensure that Singaporeans from all socio-economic backgrounds will have access to essential medical care when they fall ill.
